title: PCB-B COMPUTE

pair_passes.note: 100 ohm: on In2/In3 the field solver reads 102 ohm at a 0.127 gap, inside tolerance, and the envelope is 0.387 against the 0.46 it uses outside, so this class gains both layers and room
90 ohm: stays on the outer layers, where its class geometry already hits the target; 0.127/0.127 on In2/In3 would read 102 ohm against a 90 ohm target

finish._cont_route_why: 11 September 2026: one continuation pass of the router before the stub router when a handful of connections are open (A21's lever of 5 September). cont_route.sh keeps the board only if it improves, so it cannot make one worse; it was declared for A alone because only the A clones carried it, and E and P both ended a route at exactly one open.
finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.

_pair_env_why: 13 September 2026, THE CURVE WAS RE-MEASURED ON THE TOOLS THAT LAY THE PAIRS TODAY, which is what the note it replaces asked for in capitals. What moved since the 12 September sweep: the pair's end emissions are asked about the partner BEFORE they are laid and move their approach into the pad when the last hop is the violation (PAIR_END_FIT, appendix 32.173), and that alone took this board from 38 to 54 of 113 at the old 0.06. Re-swept with it on, one placed board, one variable, eight arms: 0.04 lays 64 (32 DIFF100 + 32 USB), 0.05 lays 64 (35 + 29), 0.06 lays 54 (35 + 19), 0.07 lays 64 (34 + 30), 0.08 lays 65 (37 + 28), 0.09 lays 60 (34 + 26), 0.10 lays 62 (34 + 28), 0.12 lays 58 (32 + 26). The peak has MOVED to 0.08 and the old declared 0.06 is now the WORST point of the sweep: its DIFF100 pass lays 35, as good as any, and leaves the USB pass 19 where every neighbour leaves it 26 to 32, which is the greedy pass showing its shape. The value here is 0.08 with that table as its reason, and the caution stands unchanged: re-measure the whole curve when the tools or the placement move.
_pair_via_mode_why: 12 September 2026, measured on B19's placed board (md5 f8b5828a9d4e), DIFF100 only, four arms. The class via of DIFF100 is 0.70 mm, so the pair's own two vias need 0.70 + 0.127 = 0.827 mm centre to centre, and the HDMI and Ethernet fans this board leaves from are on an 0.8 mm pitch: 36 of the 74 failed attempts in one 48-pair pass were the pair refused for its own two vias, every one reading 0.707 to 0.800 of 0.822. At the board's own via minimum (0.40/0.20, which escape.py has laid at fine pitch here since 5 September) the demand falls to 0.522. Arms: alphabet-and-span order 8 -> 14 of 48, contention `scarce` order 11 -> 15 of 48. Worth +6 and +4, which is less than the twenty predicted and more than any other single knob measured on this board since the slack. Declared for B and not as the tool's default, because it is measured on B: A lays 3 of 3 with the class via at a 2.54 mm ribbon, where the arithmetic does not bind.
_phase_why: B21, 16 September 2026. B19's route was stopped at nine and a half hours, two passes of twenty, because the board it was routing is missing the six PCIe receive coupling capacitors the CM5 datasheet requires (section 2.3.1, 220 nF before the IC): the generator was corrected at 02:40 on 16 September and B has not been regenerated since, so its netlist still runs PCIE1_RX_P straight from U101 pin 124 to U30B pin 116. Those capacitors are IN SERIES in the receive lines, so no amount of routing on the old board reaches the new one, and the cross-board contract that holds the shape fails on every board of the set until B is rebuilt. This is the three-resistor lesson of 15 September in a bigger place: a route on a superseded design is not a deliverable, and the cheapest moment to say so is the first one. B20 was a placement arm that was measured and stopped and never cut; the phase after B19 is therefore B21. 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh s 17 SEPTEMBER 2026, THE DECLARATION IS THE BOARD IN THIS TREE AND NOT THE ROUTE IN FLIGHT. It was set to the in-flight phase on 16 September with the reason that final_gate refuses a folder that is not the declared one, and that is exactly what went wrong: every reader that GATES on this field asks 'is this folder the board', so pointing it at a route that has not landed makes those gates answer about a board that does not exist. Board P proved the cost: its P4 folder holds the board this tree holds, byte for byte (sha256 d79865e7b1aceb95), and it was being read as stale against a declared P5 that was measured, refused and abandoned under decision 28. Board A declared A36, a route that was never cut, while the tree carries A32. The phase in flight belongs to the RUN (`routeflow --phase`, with ROUTEFLOW_PHASE_UNDECLARED=1 for an arm whose board may never be adopted), and it moves into this field in the same commit that brings the board in.
_place_env_why: 12 September 2026 (appendix 32.146, 32.147). 30 of 46 leg refusals on B19's DIFF100 pass sat within 2 mm of one of the pair's OWN pads and 22 of those at the pairs' own series coupling capacitors, which the packer stacks as couples at its global 1.2 mm gap. Two placements regenerated on the same tools, one at 1.2 and one at 2.4, each with its own chain and gate: the DIFF100 pass lays 14 of 48 at 1.2 and 22 of 48 at 2.4, and the leg-fit refusals go from 102 lines to 8 with the 76 that were refused out in the corridor becoming none. The escape quality is unchanged (1,493 escapes and 279 skipped pads against 1,488 and 284), so the pairs are not bought at the fine-pitch parts' expense. A placement change moves every part in its region, so this is recorded as one placement against another rather than as a knob with a value. ** 15 September 2026 23:10 CEST, the B placement loop measured five values and the declaration goes back to 2.4: the loop's own pass ran without PAIR_COVER_LEGS and PAIR_CLASS_CLEAR (fixed at 22:39), and on the production pass the 2.6 placement lays 31 of 48 DIFF100 pairs where B19's own chain laid 35 at 2.4; the same 2.6 placed board laid 38 in the loop's arm and 33 in three reproductions (the placement is deterministic, four regenerations identical; the escape stage is not, one GND via differed, and a greedy pass without rip-up turns one cell into five pairs, appendix 32.117). So no value of this knob is distinguishable from the pass's own scatter by a single arm; 2.8 and 3.2 are ILLEGAL (mask bridges at the antenna jacks), PLACE_GAP 1.8 and PLACE_PTH_OBSTACLE 1 are ILLEGAL on the placed board, PLACE_FINE_MARGIN 2.6 and PLACE_NO_UNDER_FINE 1 are refused by the region gate. couple_gap.py reads the achieved gap back: 2.4 reads 1.80 mm between the parts' boxes.
_pair_cover_legs_why: 13 September 2026, measured on B19 at the declared baseline (end fit on, slack 0.08), one variable: PAIR_COVER_LEGS=0 lays 65 of 113 (37 DIFF100 + 28 USB), =1 lays 71 (38 + 33). The corridor is grown by w + s/2 + slack and the legs by w + s/2 + 0.02, so the corridor is 0.02 mm short of covering its own legs and the whole margin at the standard slack is one grid cell (appendix 32.126, 11 September). It was worth +1 on the tools of that day and OFF on the reading that it costs 0.12 mm of envelope; with the end fit laying the last hop properly it is worth SIX, which is the record's own law about removing the last bar rather than a bar. The slack was re-swept with it on: 0.06 lays 63, 0.08 lays 71, 0.10 lays 57, 0.12 lays 63, so 0.08 remains the peak and PAIR_LEG_RETRY=2 on top of it costs nine (62).
_pair_passes_order_why: 14 September 2026, measured on today's tools at the declared baseline (end fit, cover legs, slack 0.08): DIFF100 first lays 71 of 113 (38 + 33), USB first lays 55 (28 DIFF100 + 27 USB). The record's number for the reverse order was 56 against 60 on the tools of 10 September, so the direction has held through three generations of the tool while the size of the gap has grown. DIFF100 goes first because it is the pass that takes the extra layers, and what it lays is what the second pass has to route around.
_pair_class_clear_why: 14 September 2026, MEASURED AND DECLARED FOR B. The pre-router's occupancy map grew every obstacle by the module literal CLR = 0.16 mm, whatever class it belongs to and whatever class the pair belongs to, on every board. B19's DIFF100 and USB classes ask for 0.127, and the escape fans the legs have to reach their own vias through are laid at 0.127 with 0.127 tracks, so a 0.254 mm lane loses a quarter of its width to margin that KiCad's own rule does not ask for: the clearance between two items is the LARGER of their two classes'. Two arms, one variable, the same placed board, at this board's declared baseline: the map as it was lays 62 of 113 (35 DIFF100 + 27 USB) and the class-aware map lays 64 (37 + 27). Plus two, and it is the correct model rather than a lever, which is why it is declared here rather than argued about. AND A CORRECTION TO CARRY: the control arm says 62, where the record's baseline for this board was 71 measured yesterday evening. The generators moved between the two, so 71 is not reproducible on today's tree and every comparison from here is against 62. The caution of 32.109 word for word: the baseline also moved because the board did.
_pair_coupled_fraction_why: 15 September 2026 02:40 CEST, OWNER RULING, his words: 'while B is blocked on your decision == unblock B from my decision'. Decision 24 became the session's and the session took its option 2, the one the decision itself recommended: the board passes the pair hold when the coupled length across its judged pairs is at least this fraction of the total, every pair still named with its own verdict, the 1 mm length gate untouched for the pairs that exist. The number: B lays 62 to 71 of 113 pairs on the tools of the day (32.174, 32.185), ruling 18's floor plan is refused by the board by 86.2 mm, and USB 2.0's own budget for uncoupled length is a sixteenth of the edge, so 80 percent of the pair copper coupled and the rest laid by the router as two traces is the measured board rather than a hoped-for one. What this changes is the bar; the read-back of every pair is unchanged and stays in the record.
_gate_before_placement_why: 15 September 2026: check_pcb_b carries the I/O high-availability topology checks of 9 September (each bank's home and failover host, the selects reaching both switches), and on the MECHANICAL board, 27 footprints and no placement, every one of them reads an empty list: 52 FAIL lines and 'RESULT: 52 FAIL' before the placement runs and the same gate passes 2142 of 2142 after it. routeflow's pre-route judge blocks on any FAIL line in the log, so B19 has been unrunnable under routeflow since those checks were written, and nobody saw it because every B measurement since ran as an arm whose driver reads only the pair count. C, D, E and P run no gate before placement; B joins them, and the gate that means something runs where it always has, on the placed board.
_place_audit_gate_off_why: 15 September 2026, B19's first route for a deliverable under the delegated decision 24. The placement predictor names 9 collisions among 75 fine-pitch parts (U19, U20, U7, U102, U209: pads whose escape fan could not be placed), the same stations 32.146 measured as the pair wall, and B18 routed with the gate off on 9 September for the same reason. The route decides what the predictor predicts: the routed-board gate, hard 0 of fifteen types and 0 unrouted, is unchanged.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins. Board B carries every fast interface in the kit, so most of this table is strict and the slow entries are the exceptions, which is the opposite of the other six boards.

_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): six layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
_via_ring_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, the VIA rows rather than the annular ring row. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): minimum via diameter 0.25 mm on a minimum via hole of 0.15 mm for 2 or more layers, which leaves 0.05 mm of copper per side. The PTH annular ring row (0.20 mm) is stated for a plated COMPONENT hole and cannot bind a via, because no via at this document's own minimum could satisfy it; board D12 was refused on 16 September for a 0.45/0.20 via at 0.125 mm of ring, which is what that confusion costs.
_copper_layers_why: Six layers, and this is the one board of the set whose layer count stands on its own measurement: three compute modules at 0.4 mm receptacle pitch need two inner signal layers, and a board-wide In1 keep-out left 93 opens at eight passes.

the Power over Ethernet feed, which leaves the case on that same wall jack

_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. A port that leaves the ENCLOSURE is a wire a person will plug something into, in the rain, having walked across a floor. Every one of them reaches a semiconductor, and the only thing between is a suppressor, a choke, a series resistor into a clamp, or nothing. Most connectors on these boards are internal (board-to-board ribbons, module sockets, fan leads inside a sealed case) and treating every J as external would refuse every board for wires that never leave it. The board knows which is which and nothing else does, so each one is named with where it goes.

GND.what: the board's single ground: every return on this board is this net

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k

_escape_gap_why: MEASURED 17 September 2026, and a hypothesis refused. B21's placement predicts ten escape-fan collisions (U101 38 of 99 pads without an escape, U301 34, U202 17, U302 14, U7 12 of 24, U19 5 of 14), and the escape pass's own debug lines name a via of the PAD'S OWN NET as the last thing it rejected at several of them, which reads like a false refusal: same-net copper needs no clearance and the escape would only have to reach a via that is already there. It is not. Counted over the whole placed board: 560 fine-pitch pads have no escape and only 12 of them have a via of their own net within 0.5 mm, 17 within 1.0 and 35 within 2.0. The 'last reject' line is the last of many candidate positions and not a statement about the pad's neighbourhood, which is the 8 September lesson about a debug print that does not share the predicate it explains. So place_audit is not describing its own limit here and the prediction stands: this board's fine-pitch fans do not fit where they are, which is a PLACEMENT item for B22 and not a tool item. AND THE ROOM IT WOULD TAKE IS MEASURED (17 September 2026, 16:20 CEST). The knob that gives a fine-pitch part more room is PLACE_FINE_MARGIN, whose own note carries 10 September's reading (194 pads with no escape at 1.6 mm against 69 at 2.6, and 50 pairs of 113 against 43). Re-run on today's tools in its own tree, the 2.6 mm arm does not reach the pair pass at all: the region-fit gate REFUSES the placement with nine regions over their rectangles, S1_SWIC by 13.9 mm, S2_SWIC by 5.7, S3_SWIC by 3.7, ETH by 2.9, GAP12 by 2.6, IOCA and RADE by 1.8 and the two rail pockets by 1.0. At the declared 1.6 nothing overflows. So the answer to 'give the fans room' is not a knob: it is owner ruling 13's resize, one region at a time with its overflow before and after, and those nine numbers are the work list. The baseline to beat is 11 predicted collisions of 75 fine-pitch parts and 31 of 68 pairs laid, both taken on 17 September.
_floor_plan_room_why: WHERE THE ROOM IS, MEASURED (17 September 2026, region_room.py on the regenerated placement). The three pockets that need it have none: S1_SWIC has 0.0 mm in all four directions (a fixed hole west, S1_SWE east, S1_RAIL south, the M.2 socket J_M2 north), S2_SWIC 0.0 in all four, boxed by regions on every side, and S3_SWIC 1.0 mm west and nothing else. The room on this board is elsewhere: ETH has 49.0 mm to its south before it meets BATT, IOCA 22.0 mm north, RADE 11.5 mm south, S1_RAIL 6.0 mm west, IOCA 5.0 mm west to the outline, ETH 3.0 mm west, GAP12 3.0 mm north. So the escape-fan problem on this board CANNOT be solved by growing the switch pockets: they are boxed in, and the answer is a redistribution, parts moving out of the three per-slot pockets into the regions that have room, which is the 'floor plan built around the pair corridors' the record has named since 10 September. The numbers above are where that campaign starts. THE WHOLE TABLE, for the campaign to start from: in the slot column band the only front-side slack is S1_SWE and S3_SWE with 12.5 mm to the north (S2_SWE has none north and 3.0 south), and S2_SUP has 5.0 mm north; the BACK-side rail pockets are roomy (S1_RAILB 19.0 west into IOCA, S2_RAILB 16.0 east, S3_RAILB 16.0 west) and so are POEB 63.0 south, ETH 49.0 south, WIFISW 38.5 north and 14.0 south, IOCA 22.0 north. Every SWIC pocket is bounded north by the M.2 socket and east by its own SWE, so the only way to widen one is to move the SWIC/SWE boundary east and let SWE take its 12.5 mm northward, which is a two-region move on one slot and is what owner ruling 13's procedure asks to be reported before and after.
_floor_plan_targets_why: WHERE THE TWO PROBLEMS MEET, counted on B21 (17 September 2026). The pair pass laid 31 of 68 and its failures die at: U32B and U31B twelve times each, U301 twelve, U4 and U3 ten, U1 ten, U30B six, U209 six, U302 four, U109 four, U102 four, then J_M2N3, J_M2C3 and J_HDMI. The escape fans that cannot be placed are at U101 (36 of 99 pads), U301 (37), U201 (30), U102 (21), U202 (19), U302 (16), U209 (16), U7 (12 of 24), U19 (5) and U20 (3). FOUR PARTS ARE IN BOTH LISTS: U301, U302, U209 and U102, the slot-3 PCIe switch, its hub and the slot-2 pair of the same, and the pair failures otherwise concentrate at the CM5 receptacles' high-speed halves (U30B, U31B, U32B) and at the switch U1 and the display switches U3 and U4. So the corridor from a module receptacle to its own switch and hub is the thing the floor plan has to serve, and it is the same copper the fans need: that is why the two knobs do not compose and why the answer is a layout rather than a margin.
_floor_plan_resize_why: OWNER RULING 13'S SECOND PASS: THE NINE REGIONS THE 2.6 MM FINE MARGIN OVERFLOWS, EACH WITH ITS OVERFLOW BEFORE AND AFTER (17 September 2026, one tree and one instrument, the two generators and the region table, nothing routed and nothing committed to the board). ETH 2.92 -> 0 with 4 mm south (49.0 mm of room before BATT). IOCA 1.78 -> 0 with 3 mm north (22.0). RADE 1.81 -> 0 with 3 mm south (11.5). GAP12 2.61 -> 0.11 with 2.5 mm north and -> 0 with 2 mm west as well. S1_RAIL 1.01 -> 0 by taking 2 mm of height from S1_SUP, and its own 2 mm of width west bought NOTHING (1.01 either way); S3_RAIL 1.01 -> 0 the same way, its 0.75 mm of width east buying nothing. S1_SWIC 12.74 -> 3.69 with 6 mm of width from S1_SWE, which takes its measured 12 mm north, -> 0.69 with 3 mm of height and -> 0 with 4. S3_SWIC 3.69 -> 0 with 3 mm of width and 4 of height, the width alone buying nothing. S2_SWIC 5.69 -> 0 with 8 mm of width, S2_SWE taking 6 mm south to pay for it. The three SWIC pockets are boxed north by the M.2 socket, so their height comes through a chain, SWIC from RAIL and RAIL from SUP, and at 2.6 that chain needs the 3 mm band between S1_SUP and S3_SUP and the board outline, which would put parts at the edge and is refused. At 2.0 the whole board fits with none of that. A TRAP WORTH THE RECORD: a region grown all the way to what stops it packs WORSE, because the obstacle is then inside the rectangle and the shelf packer must step around it: S2_SUP2 grown its measured 1 mm north went from 0.55 mm over to 3.57, and grown 2 mm east to 6.57. Leave a margin or do not grow. AND THE TRADE THE RESIZE WAS FOR, measured with the whole pre-route chain to the placed board, the predictor on each: today's rectangles at the declared 1.6 predict ELEVEN escape-fan collisions of 75 fine-pitch parts with 1465 escapes and 288 pads skipped; the resized rectangles at 1.6 predict THIRTEEN (1451 and 302), so the resize alone COSTS two; the resized rectangles at 2.0 buy the escapes it was all for, 1491 and 264, and produce a placement with TWENTY-NINE hard violations, every one a front part over U52 or U62, the five SWD pins of the two underside controllers, which this schematic calls SWD PADS and draws as a through-hole 1x5 header. A through-hole pad occupies both sides, so a debug header on the underside is a keep-out on the front that nothing declares: it is decision 11's finding again, one board later. WITH THAT ONE FOOTPRINT ON A SURFACE-MOUNT LAND (PinHeader_1x05_P2.54mm_Vertical_SMD_Pin1Left, one line of gen_sch_b.py, nothing else changed) the 2.0 arm reads 1496 escapes, 259 pads skipped and TEN predicted collisions, which beats today's eleven, and its hard set falls from 29 to FIVE, all five being pads of one part, U24, inside a rule area at (284.75, 110.0). That is one part's seat and it is what B22's generation starts from. PLACE_PTH_OBSTACLE, refused twice before because the packer had nowhere to step, is FREE on the resized floor plan at 1.6 (0 hard, no overflow, the same 1451 and 302 as without it) and costs GAP12 3.49 mm at 2.0, which GAP12 has not got. None of this is applied to the generator while B21 is routing: the rectangles, the margin and the SWD land are one change and they belong to B22, with these numbers as its baseline to beat.
